sites.name: IM-2 Athena (Intuitive Machines, landed 2025-03-06)
sites.note: Landed point (lander on its side in a ~20 m crater on Mons Mouton). Intended site 84.78 S, 29.13 E (LROC).
sites.source: LROC (NASA/GSFC/ASU) featured image 'IM-2 Athena Seen Obliquely' (2025): Athena at 84.7906 S, 29.1957 E

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus (Intuitive Machines, landed 2024-02-22)
sites.note: Landed point near Malapert A; coordinates published to 0.01 deg only.
sites.source: LROC featured image 'Intuitive Machines IM-1 On The Moon!' (2024): Odysseus at 80.13 S, 1.44 E, 2579 m

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram (Statio Shiv Shakti, landed 2023-08-23)
sites.note: Landed point. High southern latitude but not polar: Sun and Earth rise well above the horizon.
sites.source: IAU/USGS Gazetteer 'Statio Shiv Shakti' (69.3734 S, 32.3198 E, approved 2024-03-19); LROC independently: 69.3741 S, 32.32 E, 532 m

sites.name: Shackleton-de Gerlache connecting ridge, point C1
sites.note: Mazarico et al. (2011) 'Site 1' (89.45 S, 222.69 E; 89.0% on a 240 m DEM) is the same ridge point. Published illumination depends strongly on DEM resolution, period and observer height (same point: 76% at 20 m/px vs 89% at 240 m/px); compare with tolerance ~10 percentage points.
sites.source: Glaser, P. et al. (2018) Illumination conditions at the lunar poles: implications for future exploration, Planet. Space Sci. 162, 170-178, Table 1 (Connecting Ridge C1, surface level, 2017-2037): 76.0%

sites.name: Connecting ridge, point C2
sites.note: Published illumination depends strongly on DEM resolution, period and observer height (same point: 76% at 20 m/px vs 89% at 240 m/px); compare with tolerance ~10 percentage points.
sites.source: Glaser et al. (2018) PSS 162, Table 1 (Connecting Ridge C2, surface level, 2017-2037): 75.6%

sites.name: Shackleton crater rim, point S
sites.note: Mazarico et al. (2011): 86.7% at 89.78 S, 204.27 E (240 m DEM). Published illumination depends strongly on DEM resolution, period and observer height (same point: 76% at 20 m/px vs 89% at 240 m/px); compare with tolerance ~10 percentage points.
sites.source: Glaser et al. (2018) PSS 162, Table 1 (Shackleton S, surface level, 2017-2037): 81.0%

sites.name: de Gerlache crater rim, max-illumination pixel
sites.note: Point selected by us as the brightest 60 m pixel on the de Gerlache rim; it lies inside NASA's 2022 'de Gerlache Rim' region (Barker et al. 2021 'Site 11' is on this rim but its numeric coordinates were not available to us). Published illumination depends strongly on DEM resolution, period and observer height (same point: 76% at 20 m/px vs 89% at 240 m/px); compare with tolerance ~10 percentage points.
sites.source: NASA GSFC PGDA / LOLA PDS product AVGVISIB_85S_060M_201608 (Mazarico et al. 2011 method; 18.6-yr hourly average, 60 m/px): maximum on the de Gerlache rim (annulus 10-22 km from the IAU crater centre) = 82.7%

sites.name: Shackleton crater floor (PSR)
sites.note: Crater-centre point on the ~6.6 km flat floor; every 60 m pixel within +-120 m is PSR in the PGDA map.
sites.source: IAU/USGS Gazetteer crater centre 'Shackleton' (89.67 S, 129.78 E, D=20.9 km); floor permanently shadowed: Zuber et al. 2012 Nature 486, 378; Mazarico et al. 2011 PSR map (PGDA LPSR_85S_060M_201608 = 1 here)

sites.name: Haworth crater floor (PSR)
sites.note: Crater-centre point on the shadowed floor; every 60 m pixel within +-120 m is PSR in the PGDA map.
sites.source: IAU/USGS Gazetteer crater centre 'Haworth' (87.45 S, 354.83 E, D=51.4 km); permanently shadowed per PGDA LPSR_85S_060M_201608 (Mazarico et al. 2011 method)
